title: Careers in Sports Management: 10 Jobs, What They Pay, and How to Break In
summary: Explore 10 careers in sports management, from partnerships and ticket sales to analytics. See 2025 BLS salaries and a step-by-step plan to break in.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


• Careers in sports management cover the business side of sports: marketing, partnerships, ticket sales, events, venues, communications, athlete representation, college athletics and analytics. BLS 2025 medians run from $47,320 for coaches to $166,790 for marketing managers.


• This guide breaks down 10 sports management jobs, what each one looks like day to day, and who hires for them.


• You'll see real 2025 salary data, including what the same jobs pay inside pro sports organizations: often 20% to 37% less for marketing, sales and PR roles.


• You'll get the 2026 hiring trends in college athletics, a step-by-step plan to break in with no experience, and the skills teams actually screen for.


[Externships](https://www.extern.com/post/what-is-an-externship) are short, remote professional experience programs where you work on real projects for real companies, with guidance from people in the field. The[Breaking Games Performance Marketing & Growth Strategy Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/breaking-games-performance-marketing-growth-strategy-nov-2026) and the[Breaking Games Social Media Coordinator Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/breaking-games-social-media-coordinator-nov-2026) give you marketing and content work you can show a sports team.[Explore all Externships](https://www.extern.com/externships) .


---


## What Is Sports Management, Really?


**Sports management** is the business side of sports: selling tickets and sponsorships, marketing teams and athletes, running games and venues, negotiating contracts, and managing college athletic programs. If you're looking at careers in sports management, you're looking at the front office, not the field. The people who make a game happen, not the people who play it.


But that front office is bigger than most students think. Pro teams are only one slice. College athletic departments, leagues, sports agencies, sportswear and media brands, arenas, racing teams and esports organizations all hire for the same core skills.


The Bureau of Labor Statistics puts some numbers on it. The median annual wage for[entertainment and sports occupations](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/entertainment-and-sports/home.htm) was $59,400 in May 2025, above the $50,980 median for all occupations, and BLS projects about 91,100 openings a year in the group through 2035.


Here's what we've noticed in thousands of one-on-one sessions with students who want to work in sports. The ones who get hired usually aren't the biggest fans in the room. They're the ones who can point to something they've already done: a sales result, a content portfolio, a data project. Passion gets you to apply. Proof gets you the interview.


## What Are the Best Careers in Sports Management?


There's no single "sports management job." Below are 10 roles that hire sports management grads (and plenty of business, marketing and communications grads too), with pay data from the closest BLS occupation.


### Sports Marketing Manager


**Sports marketing managers** turn fans into revenue. They plan campaigns for ticket packages, run social and email promotions, and work with creative teams on game-day experiences. Most start as marketing or social media coordinators and work up.


The BLS median pay for[marketing managers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/advertising-promotions-and-marketing-managers.htm) was $166,790 in 2025, with 6% projected growth from 2025 to 2035. Keep in mind that number reflects experienced managers across every industry. Inside spectator sports (pro and semi-pro teams, leagues and racetracks), BLS[industry data](https://www.bls.gov/oes/tables.htm) puts the May 2025 median at $123,230. Brand-side marketing at[Nike](https://www.extern.com/post/nike-internship-guide) ,[adidas](https://www.extern.com/post/adidas-internship-guide) ,[Under Armour](https://www.extern.com/post/under-armour-internship-guide) or[Fanatics](https://www.extern.com/post/fanatics-internship-guide) is another route into the same work. Want a project to show? The[Breaking Games Performance Marketing & Growth Strategy Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/breaking-games-performance-marketing-growth-strategy-nov-2026) has you work out which ad dollars actually turn into sales, which is the same question every team marketing department asks.


### Corporate Partnerships and Sponsorship Manager


Partnerships managers sell sponsorship deals (jersey patches, arena naming, in-game promotions) and then make sure the sponsor gets what they paid for. That second part, called activation and ROI reporting, is where a lot of the real work happens.


This is one of the best-paid paths on the business side because it's sales, and sales scales. Students on Extern have worked on sponsorship strategy and ROI projects with NY Racing, a NASCAR team, which is exactly this skill set. League offices hire for it too: see our[NFL](https://www.extern.com/post/nfl-internship-guide) ,[NBA](https://www.extern.com/post/nba-internship-guide) ,[MLB](https://www.extern.com/post/mlb-internship-guide) ,[NHL](https://www.extern.com/post/nhl-internship-guide) and[WNBA](https://www.extern.com/post/wnba-internship-guide) guides. For current openings, our[sports internships guide](https://www.extern.com/post/sports-internships-summer-2027-guide) tracks partnerships roles at teams and leagues.


### Ticket Sales and Sales Manager


Ticket sales is the most common door into a team front office. Seriously. And teams hire entry-level sales reps in groups, train them, and promote the strong ones into account management, premium seating or partnerships.


According to the BLS,[sales managers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/sales-managers.htm) earned a median of $148,270 in 2025. But inside spectator sports, that median falls to $96,670, and sales reps for services in the industry earn a median of $47,580 (BLS, May 2025). That's usually a base salary plus commission, so treat sales as a launchpad, not a destination you're stuck in. Ticketing companies hire for this too; here's our[Ticketmaster internship guide](https://www.extern.com/post/ticketmaster-internship-guide) .


### Event and Game Operations Coordinator


Game operations people make sure everything on a game day actually happens: staffing, security, timing, halftime shows, the national anthem, the T-shirt cannon. Tournaments, marathons and college championships hire for the same work.


BLS groups this with[meeting, convention, and event planners](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/meeting-convention-and-event-planners.htm) , who earned a median of $61,160 in 2025, with 6% projected growth through 2035. Inside spectator sports the median is lower, at $49,110. So expect nights and weekends. That's the job. Motorsports is a big employer here; see our[NASCAR](https://www.extern.com/post/nascar-internship-guide) and[Hendrick Motorsports](https://www.extern.com/post/hendrick-motorsports-internship-guide) guides.


### Facility and Venue Manager


Venue managers run stadiums, arenas and training facilities: maintenance, scheduling, safety, vendor contracts and non-sports events like concerts. It's an operations role that rewards people who stay calm when something breaks at 6 p.m. before a sold-out game.


The BLS median for facilities managers was $106,660 in 2025, according to its[administrative services and facilities managers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/administrative-services-managers.htm) profile. It's one of the few roles where sports pays close to the market rate: facilities managers inside spectator sports earned a median of $102,990. Most venue managers get there after years in event operations or facility roles, not straight out of school.


### Sports Communications and PR Specialist


Sports PR and communications staff handle media requests, set up player interviews, write press releases, manage team social channels and step in when there's a crisis. It's fast, public and very deadline-driven.


The BLS lists a median of $74,750 for[public relations specialists](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/media-and-communication/public-relations-specialists.htm) in 2025, with 2% projected growth through 2035, which is slower than most roles here. And inside spectator sports, the median is just $47,230, the biggest gap of any role in this guide. And media companies are the other big employer; see our[Fox Corporation internship guide](https://www.extern.com/post/fox-corporation-internship-guide) . Content skills give you an edge. The[Breaking Games Social Media Coordinator Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/breaking-games-social-media-coordinator-nov-2026) has you make real short-form videos and a social ad concept for your portfolio.


### Sports Agent


Sports agents represent athletes. They negotiate contracts, find endorsement deals and help manage a client's career. In the major U.S. leagues, players' unions certify agents and set limits on what they can charge, and the work is mostly commission-based.


So agent income is unpredictable, especially early on. And it's a small field. BLS counts about 12,620 agents and business managers of artists, performers and athletes nationwide, with a May 2025 median of $82,890. Most people start as an assistant at an agency and handle research, marketing or client service. If that path interests you, read our guides to[Excel Sports Management](https://www.extern.com/post/excel-sports-management-internship-guide) ,[CAA Sports](https://www.extern.com/post/caa-sports-internship-guide) and[Octagon](https://www.extern.com/post/octagon-internship-guide) internships, plus[Wasserman](https://www.extern.com/post/wasserman-internship-guide) and[Endeavor](https://www.extern.com/post/endeavor-internship-guide) , the agencies students ask about most.


### Athletic Director and College Athletics Administrator


College athletic departments employ a lot of people outside of coaching: compliance officers, academic advisors, roster and revenue-share staff, ticket and marketing teams, and fundraisers. Our[NCAA internship guide](https://www.extern.com/post/ncaa-internship-guide) covers the governing-body side. The athletic director runs the whole operation and answers to the university.


BLS doesn't have a separate athletic director category. The closest one,[postsecondary education administrators](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/postsecondary-education-administrators.htm) , had a median of $104,590 in 2025. Athletic fundraising is its own path too:[fundraisers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/fundraisers.htm) earned a median of $72,550, with 6% projected growth.


### Sports Data and Business Analyst


Sports analytics isn't just player stats. Teams use analysts to price tickets, segment fans, measure sponsor value and forecast attendance. If you like spreadsheets and sports, this is the fastest-growing corner of the business side.


The BLS reports a median of $78,760 for[market research analysts](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/market-research-analysts.htm) in 2025, with 7% projected growth from 2025 to 2035. Here's the part most guides miss. Data roles take the smallest pay cut for working in sports: data scientists in spectator sports earned a median of $103,860 in May 2025, only about 14% below the all-industry median of $120,230. SQL is the skill that keeps showing up in job posts. The[Breaking Games SQL & Database Architecture Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/breaking-games-sql-database-architecture-nov-2026) has you turn messy sales files into a working database and dashboard.


### Coach or Scout


Plenty of sports management majors still want to be closer to the field. Coaches teach athletes skills and strategy, and scouts evaluate players for recruiting or the draft.


According to the BLS,[coaches and scouts](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/entertainment-and-sports/coaches-and-scouts.htm) earned a median of $47,320 in 2025, with 6% projected growth and about 36,400 openings a year through 2035. Yet a lot of those openings are part-time high school and youth roles, which probably explains most of that lower median. Coaches and scouts working for pro and semi-pro organizations earned a median of $62,570.


## How Much Do Sports Management Jobs Pay?


Sports management pay ranges from about $47,000 for coaches to well over $140,000 for experienced sales and marketing managers, based on 2025 BLS medians. The business roles (sales, marketing, partnerships) pay the most. But the same jobs pay noticeably less when the employer is a sports organization, so the table shows both numbers.


Sports management role Closest BLS occupation Median pay, all industries (2025) Median pay, spectator sports (May 2025) Projected growth, 2025-35


**Sports marketing manager** Marketing managers $166,790 $123,230 6%


**Partnerships / sponsorship manager** Sales managers $148,270 $96,670 4%


**Ticket sales manager** Sales managers $148,270 $96,670 4%


**Facility / venue manager** Facilities managers $106,660 $102,990 5% (admin services & facilities group)


**Athletic director / college administrator** Postsecondary education administrators $104,590 n/a (college athletics is not in this industry) 2%


**Sports data / business analyst** Market research analysts and marketing specialists $78,760 $59,540 7%


**Sports PR / communications** Public relations specialists $74,750 $47,230 2%


**Athletic fundraising** Fundraisers $72,550 $59,890 6%


**Event / game operations** Meeting, convention & event planners $61,160 $49,110 6%


**Coach or scout** Coaches and scouts $47,320 $62,570 6%


**Sports agent** Agents and business managers $82,890 $90,530 (only ~140 work directly for sports organizations) n/a


Sources: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook (all-industry medians, projections) and BLS OEWS industry data for[spectator sports, NAICS 711200](https://www.bls.gov/oes/tables.htm) , May 2025.


Now the honest part. These medians cover everyone in the occupation, across every industry and experience level. Entry-level jobs inside team front offices usually pay less than marketing or sales jobs at a regular company, because so many people want to work in sports. People in the industry call it the "passion tax," and the BLS numbers show its size. Inside spectator sports, PR specialists earn 37% less than the all-industry median, sales managers 35% less, marketing managers 26% less and event planners 20% less. But facilities managers (3% less) and data scientists (14% less) barely pay it at all. One honest caveat: nobody publishes reliable entry-level pay for team front offices specifically, so treat any single starting-salary number you see online with some suspicion.


But it isn't permanent. Or at least, it shrinks fast once you build a skill that's hard to replace, like selling partnerships or running analytics. If pure pay is your top priority, our guide to[fun jobs that pay well](https://www.extern.com/post/fun-jobs-that-pay-well-guide) is worth a look too.


## Is Sports Management a Good Major?


Sports management is a good major if you already know you want the business side of sports and you'll actually use its internships and alumni network. If you're not sure yet, a broader degree keeps more doors open. It's also a crowded field: U.S. schools awarded 17,472 sport and fitness management degrees in 2024, including 9,527 bachelor's degrees, according to[Data USA](https://datausa.io/profile/cip/sport-fitness-management) 's analysis of federal IPEDS data. Here's how the two sides stack up.


### The Case For It


• **Built-in industry access.** Many programs require internships with teams, athletic departments or events, and faculty often have front-office contacts.


• **Relevant coursework.** Sport law, facility management, sport finance and sponsorship are taught directly instead of picked up on the job.


• **A ready-made network.** Alumni working in college athletics and minor league teams tend to hire from their own programs.


### The Case Against It


• **It's narrower than it looks.** Teams and agencies also hire business, marketing, communications and data majors, often for the same roles.


• **Pivoting out can be harder.** A[business degree](https://www.extern.com/post/business-degree-career-paths-guide) or a[marketing degree](https://www.extern.com/post/what-can-you-do-with-a-marketing-degree) reads well to employers in every industry, while a sports management degree mostly signals one.


• **Grad school is optional.** Sports management graduate programs help for college athletics leadership, but most front-office roles don't require one.


Our take? The major matters less than what you do with it. A sports management student with zero projects loses to a marketing student with a strong portfolio almost every time.


## How Do You Break Into Sports Management With No Experience?


You break into sports management by starting where teams hire in volume (game days, college athletics and ticket sales) and stacking one or two real projects on top. Here's the order that works best for most students.


1. **Work game days.** Your college athletic department, a minor league team or a local marathon needs event staff. It's the fastest way to meet people who already work in sports.


2. **Apply to sports internships early.** Team and league programs fill months ahead. Use our[sports internships guide](https://www.extern.com/post/sports-internships-summer-2027-guide) for deadlines, and check the[ESPN internship guide](https://www.extern.com/post/espn-internship-guide) if media is your lane.


3. **Consider starting in sales.** Ticket and partnership sales jobs open more often than marketing jobs, and they teach the skill every front office values most.


4. **Build one project in a transferable skill.** Social content, ad performance or data work all carry over to sports. An[Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships) gives you a company-endorsed project to point to, even if the company isn't a team.


5. **Network with intent.** Use[informational interview questions](https://www.extern.com/post/informational-interview-questions-guide) and[coffee chats](https://www.extern.com/post/coffee-chat-guide) to turn LinkedIn connections into referrals. A lot of front-office roles get filled through people you know.


6. **Pick a lane.** "I love sports" isn't a career plan. "I want to sell partnerships" or "I want to run fan analytics" is.

Does real experience actually matter that much? The evidence says yes.


• In Extern's 2025 product survey of 273 students who finished a project, real-world experience was the top reason they valued the program, cited by 31%.


• Alyssa Jhingree, an Extern alum who went on to intern at McLaren Racing, put it this way: "This is the type of experience that matters when interviewing."


• Hiring managers in sports see hundreds of applicants who say they're passionate. Few of them bring a finished project.


So the takeaway is simple: experience you can show beats enthusiasm you can only describe.


## What's Changing in Sports Management Hiring in 2026?


College athletics is hiring more, and for different jobs than a year ago. Postings on the CollegeSports.jobs network rose 20.3% from January to September 2026 compared with the same months of 2025 (3,403 vs. 2,829), according to its[October 2026 market report](https://collegesports.jobs/the-college-athletics-job-market-2026-ytd-vs-2025) . The report ties the jump to the first full hiring cycle after the House settlement took effect on July 1, 2025.


And the shift is easy to see by function:


• **Revenue jobs are growing fastest.** Ticket operations postings rose 57% and sales postings 55%, more than twice the market rate.


• **Entry-level roles are growing too.** Assistant director and coordinator postings rose 38%, and entry, intern and graduate assistant postings rose 24%.


• **Rules jobs are cooling.** After a 2025 surge, NIL postings fell 32% and compliance fell 12%. Schools staffed for the new rules first, then for the new revenue.


• **New titles are appearing.** Listings now include roles like "Director, Revenue Share & NIL Operations" and "Operations Analyst for Roster Management."


The House settlement lets schools that opt in share roughly $20.5 million with athletes in 2025-26, and that cap has created a brand-new front-office job: the college general manager. ESPN has called the GM role the[new gold rush](https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/44789751/college-football-gm-new-gold-rush) in college football, with schools hiring former NFL scouts and executives to run rosters.


What does that mean for you? Sponsorship skills show up in about 16% of college athletics postings now, up from 11% a year earlier, and game-day and event experience in nearly 24%. So those are exactly the skills covered in the next section.


## What Skills Do Sports Teams Actually Hire For?


**Sports teams hire for sales, data, content, partnership measurement and event operations skills, more than sports knowledge.** Everyone applying already knows the sport. The candidates who stand out can show one of these skills with a real example, and the table below shows how to prove each one as a student.


Skill Roles that use it How to prove it as a student


**Sales and persuasion** Ticket sales, partnerships, agent Campus fundraising results, a sales role with numbers you can share, or a sponsorship pitch deck


**Data (Excel, SQL)** Sports analyst, ticket pricing, marketing A dashboard or analysis project, such as fan or sales data cleaned and visualized


**Social and video content** Marketing, communications, PR A portfolio of short-form videos or a social campaign with engagement results


**Sponsorship ROI and measurement** Partnerships, marketing A project that measures whether a campaign or sponsorship paid off


**Event operations** Game operations, venue management Game-day staffing, running a campus tournament or event


And none of these require a sports job first. That's the good news. You can build every one of them in a class project, a campus role or a remote project with a company outside sports, then bring it to a team.


From our side, students on Extern have done exactly that with companies like Breaking Games and NY Racing. If you want a head start before spring hiring,[browse open Externships](https://www.extern.com/externships) and pick one that matches the lane you chose above.


## FAQ: Careers in Sports Management


### What is the highest paying job in sports management?


Marketing managers top the BLS data: a 2025 median of $166,790 across all industries and $123,230 inside spectator sports organizations. Facilities managers and data scientists come close inside sports, at about $103,000. Agents can earn more, but commission-based pay makes their income swing widely from year to year.


### Is sports management a good major?


It's a good major if you already know you want the business side of sports and you'll use its internships and alumni network. If you're unsure, a business, marketing or communications degree keeps more doors open and still gets you hired by teams, leagues and agencies.


### Can you get a sports management job without a sports management degree?


Yes. Teams and agencies hire business, marketing, communications and data majors all the time. What matters more is proof you can do the work: sales results, a content portfolio, an analytics project or game-day experience. Your major matters less than what you can actually show.


### How do I get into sports management with no experience?


Start where teams hire in volume: game-day staff, college athletic departments and ticket sales. Add one sports internship and one project in a transferable skill such as social content or data. Then use informational interviews to turn those into referrals, because many front-office roles fill through people you know.


### What entry-level sports management jobs can I get right after college?


Common first titles are ticket sales representative, partnerships coordinator, marketing or social media coordinator, event operations assistant and athletic department assistant. Pay starts below the BLS medians for senior roles, so expect a few years of building before you reach manager-level salaries in most organizations.


### Is a sports management degree worth it?


It's worth it when you pair it with experience. The degree alone rarely gets you hired, because lots of fans apply for every front-office opening. Internships, game-day work and a portfolio of real projects are what move your application to the top of the pile.
